title: 1835 and 1904 people keep busy: jobs, breaks indoors, in at night
items: Peck at his store front and Mary Flynn at her dooryard in 1835 work through the day, go in and out of their own doors, and are in at night. Mahoney and Bardwell work the bank and the tavern yard.

In 1904 the Glessners' cooks, stable helper, maid and coachman work about the court and Eighteenth Street. They gather now and then, and go in by the service stair, the north entry or the stable doors.
While someone is in, their door offers Ask for them, as in 1812.
